quote: Anthropic is generating cash. And like, they kind of— this fact is, I would say, kind of known in the world... The overwhelming majority of tokens are profitable for everyone in the chain, everyone.

summary: Gavin Baker argues Nvidia's $500B AI compute financing platform is strategically brilliant, positions Nvidia as the central bank of AI, and that revenue-share agreements could make Nvidia a large capital-light cloud business with royalty-like income.
quote: In some ways, Nvidia is kind of becoming the central bank of AI, the Federal Reserve of AI. That is like a way to kind of conceptualize what they are doing.

summary: Sacks argues Jensen's AI compute financing initiative is brilliant because it removes the financing constraint on TAM, allowing Nvidia to grow as large as actual demand by enabling downstream customers like xAI to fund massive CapEx buildouts.
quote: the numbers are getting so big that the TAM is getting constrained by the ability to finance this buildout. And what he's doing is alleviating that finance constraint so that he can grow as big as the TAM actually is.

summary: Gavin Baker argues that Grok 4.6 is Pareto dominant on quality-to-cost benchmarks, is widely overlooked by investors relative to SpaceX's other segments, and that investors should factor it into SpaceX's valuation given the precedent of Anthropic's rapid rise.
quote: Very few of these investors talk about Grok at all. And it is Pareto dominant on a lot of measures... maybe people should start to consider Grok when they think about SpaceX.

summary: Gavin Baker believes the SpaceX story is far from over, with Grok joining Starlink, orbital compute, and terrestrial compute as underappreciated value drivers that investors are not fully pricing in.
quote: there's a lot, I think, ahead for SpaceX, so the SpaceX story isn't over.

summary: Jason argues that Zuckerberg's open-source AI strategy and direct communication via X positions Meta to become the dominant open-source AI champion, predicting Meta will have the best open-source model within a year.
quote: He is going to have the best open source model in the next year. I guarantee it here on the All-In podcast.

summary: Gavin Baker highlights that a potential Silver Lake PE bid for Workday signals enterprise software has been oversold and that the return of PE bids changes the investing landscape for the software sector, though the category has been in a prolonged downturn.
quote: the return of a private equity bid for software really changes the investing landscape... Silver Lake may be buying Workday. Workday is up 17%.

summary: Gavin Baker argues that a world with 1–3 dominant frontier AI models is a hard environment for enterprise software companies, as the chart of Workday from $300 to $100 illustrates the structural headwind the sector faces.
quote: a world where Anthropic, OpenAI, and maybe even SpaceX, are kind of the only model providers that dominate the model layer. That is a hard world for software.

summary: Guest argues America has abundant natural gas, calls it a clean/green fuel, and says the world will run on natural gas for the foreseeable future while media hysteria about data centers does a disservice to Americans.
